title: UnCorrupt: Detection and prevention of Excel-style gene-symbol corruption in scientific spreadsheets
description:
Detects Excel auto-conversion damage in supplementary spreadsheets accompanying genomics papers: gene symbols converted to dates (SEPT7 -> Sep-07), RIKEN/accession IDs coerced to floats (2310009E13 -> 2.31E+19), leading zeros stripped, decimal-comma locale collisions, unicode homoglyph substitutions, time-coercion artifacts, and the rest of the Excel pathology documented by Ziemann et al. (2016, 2021) and Koh (2022).

Validated end-to-end on three independent corpora (re-verified 2026-05-25):

  • EPMC-expanded Ziemann 2021 S2: 95.16% cell-level recall (1591/1672 verifiable cells). The 81 missed cases are upstream annotation/file-mismatch issues, not detector deficiencies. Methodology: per-file pinning via S2's Affected_file URL, classifier-aware date-back-to-gene matching via the detector's own _reverse_gene_date.
  • Ziemann 2016: 100% recall on 279/279 validatable files, Wilson 95% [0.9864, 1.000].
  • Koh 2022 replicated at 19,500-file scale across 11 high-impact genetics journals (2022-2026): 31,377 high-confidence corruption flags across 988 distinct papers. Of the 2,180 flags cross-referenced against external gene-ID registries (HGNC, MGI, ZFIN, FlyBase, WormBase, NCBI rat), post-boost precision was 100% at every user-facing confidence band >= 0.50 (326/326 at 0.55, 11/11 at 0.60, 96/96 at 0.65, all higher bands).

Ships a Frictionless Table Schema sidecar (uncorrupt schema) that prevents future corruption: identifier columns pinned to type=string with regex constraints matching the inferred registry. Any locale-aware re-import that coerces gene symbols to dates fails validation rather than silently corrupting.
references: Ziemann M, Eren Y, El-Osta A (2016). Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature. Genome Biology 17(1):177. doi:10.1186/s13059-016-1044-7

Ziemann M, Poyet P, Lawson A (2023). The five pillars of computational reproducibility: bioinformatics and beyond. Briefings in Bioinformatics 24(6):bbad375. doi:10.1093/bib/bbad375
Koh JLY (2022). Gene Updater: a Web tool that autocorrects and updates for Excel misidentified gene names. Scientific Reports 12(1):14002. doi:10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
